Live class: verbs and their objects

lessons.title: Introduction to the Noun Phrase
lessons.body:
Every English sentence is built from phrases, and the noun phrase is the one you will use most.

## In this lesson

- What a noun phrase is: a noun and the words that belong to it
- The **head noun** and what can come before it
- Why learning phrases works better than memorizing single words

**Example:** in *the two old books on the table*, the head noun is **books**. Everything else tells us more about the books.

lessons.title: Introduction to Determiners
lessons.body:
A determiner is the word that opens a noun phrase: *a*, *the*, *this*, *my*, *some*, *every*.

## In this lesson

- What determiners do: they tell us **which one** or **how many**
- A singular countable noun needs a determiner: *a book*, not ~~book~~
- The main families: articles, demonstratives, possessives and quantifiers
quiz: I bought the a book yesterday.
In the phrase "my new phone", which word is the determiner?

lessons.title: Countable and Uncountable Determiners
lessons.body:
Some determiners go only with countable nouns, some only with uncountable nouns, and some with both.

| With countable nouns | With uncountable nouns | With both |
| --- | --- | --- |
| many, a few, several | much, a little | some, any, a lot of |

**Remember:** *information*, *advice*, *furniture* and *money* are uncountable in English. We say *some advice*, never ~~an advice~~.

lessons.title: Countable Determiners: a/an, another
lessons.body:
## a or an?

The choice follows the **sound**, not the spelling.

- *a university*, *a European country* (they begin with a "y" sound)
- *an hour*, *an honest man* (the *h* is silent)
- *an MBA*, *an umbrella*

## another

*Another* means "one more" or "a different one", and it goes with a singular countable noun: *another cup*, *another day*.
quiz: Can I have another glass of water?

lessons.title: Countable Singular Determiners: each, every, either, neither
lessons.body:
These four determiners all take a **singular** noun and a **singular** verb.

- **each**: the members of a group, one by one. *Each student has a book.*
- **every**: all the members together. *Every student has a book.*
- **either**: one or the other of two. *Either day is fine.*
- **neither**: not one and not the other of two. *Neither answer is correct.*

lessons.title: Countable Plural Determiners: these, those
lessons.body:
*This* and *that* are singular. *These* and *those* are plural.

| | Near | Far |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Singular | this book | that book |
| Plural | these books | those books |
quiz: Each of the students ___ a notebook.

lessons.title: Transitive and Intransitive Verbs: Part 1
lessons.body:
A **transitive** verb needs an object. An **intransitive** verb does not take one.

- Transitive: *She **bought** a book.* (bought what? a book)
- Intransitive: *The baby **slept**.* (nothing receives the action)

Some verbs can be both: *He **reads** every night.* / *He **reads** the newspaper.*
quiz: Which sentence has a transitive verb?
The sun rises in the east.
Which verb is intransitive here? "The children laughed loudly."

lessons.title: Common Mistake: Study English vs. Study in English
lessons.body:
These two do not mean the same thing.

- **I study English.** English is the subject I am learning.
- **I study in English.** English is the language my lessons are taught in.

So a student of the English department *studies English*, and a physics student at an English-medium university *studies physics in English*.

lessons.title: Write about your day
lessons.body: Time to use what you have learned. Pay attention to your determiners (*a*, *the*, *my*, *some*) and to whether each verb needs an object.
lessons.assignment: Write 8 to 10 sentences about what you did yesterday. Underline every determiner you use. Upload your work as a PDF, a Word file or a clear photo of your notebook.

announcement.title: Welcome to English for Beginners
announcement.body:
Start with the first lesson, "Introduction to the Noun Phrase", and work down the list. Ask anything under a lesson: I read every question.

Live classes are on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday at 5:30 pm. You will find the Join button on your dashboard.

lessons.title: Modal Auxiliary: Should and Ought to
lessons.body:
*Should* and *ought to* both give advice or say what is right. In exam questions they are usually interchangeable.

- *You **should** revise every day.*
- *You **ought to** revise every day.*

**Watch the form:** *should* is followed by the bare infinitive (*should go*), while *ought* always takes *to* (*ought to go*). The negative is *ought not to*.

lessons.title: Should and Ought to + do / be doing / have done
lessons.body:
The form after the modal tells you the time.

| Form | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| should + do | advice now or in general | You should apply. |
| should + be doing | something expected to be in progress | He should be working now. |
| should + have done | a past action that did not happen (regret or criticism) | You should have applied earlier. |
quiz: You failed because you did not study. You ___ harder.
It is 10 o'clock. The exam ___ now.
"You should have told me." What does it mean?
You did not tell me, and that was wrong.

lessons.title: Could have + been / had / done
lessons.body:
*Could have* + past participle talks about a **past possibility that did not happen**.

- *She **could have passed**, but she did not sit the exam.*
- *You **could have been** hurt!*

Compare *could not have done*: it was impossible. *He **could not have known**: nobody told him.*
quiz: He ___ the job, but he did not apply.
"She could have won." Did she win?
Choose the correct form: "You could have ___ killed."

lessons.title: Noun + Adjective Phrase: Translation and Drafting
lessons.body:
In English an adjective phrase can come **after** the noun it describes. This structure appears constantly in translation and drafting questions.

- *a man **proud of his country***
- *students **eager to learn***
- *a room **full of books***

When you translate from Bangla, find the noun first, then attach the describing phrase after it.

lessons.title: Reduced Adjective Clause: Participle Phrase
lessons.body:
An adjective clause can often be shortened to a participle phrase.

- Active: *The man **who is standing** there is my uncle.* becomes *The man **standing** there is my uncle.*
- Passive: *The book **which was written** by Tagore is famous.* becomes *The book **written** by Tagore is famous.*

**Rule of thumb:** active meaning takes *-ing*, passive meaning takes the past participle.
quiz: Reduce the clause: "The boy who is playing there is my brother."
The boy played there is my brother.
The boy playing there is my brother.
The boy plays there is my brother.
Reduce the clause: "The letter which was sent yesterday has arrived."
The letter sending yesterday has arrived.
The letter sent yesterday has arrived.
The letter was sent yesterday has arrived.
"The students ___ for the BCS need strong grammar."

lessons.title: Figures of Speech: Simile, Metaphor, Personification, Euphemism, Oxymoron
lessons.body:
Five figures of speech that come up again and again in the Preliminary test.

| Figure | What it does | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Simile | compares with *like* or *as* | as brave as a lion |
| Metaphor | says one thing **is** another | Life is a journey. |
| Personification | gives human qualities to things | The wind whispered. |
| Euphemism | a mild word for a harsh one | He passed away. |
| Oxymoron | two opposite words together | a deafening silence |
quiz: "He is as brave as a lion." Which figure of speech is this?
"The camel is the ship of the desert." Which figure of speech is this?
"He passed away last night." Which figure of speech is this?

lessons.title: Practice set: modals and participle phrases
lessons.body: A written practice set in the style of the written test. Take your time and check each sentence against the rules from this section.
lessons.assignment: 1. Write five sentences with "should have" or "could have" about a decision you regret. 2. Rewrite five sentences of your own, reducing an adjective clause to a participle phrase. Upload your answers as a PDF, a Word file or a clear photo.

announcement.title: Welcome to English for Job Seekers
announcement.body:
The lessons are recorded, so learn at your own pace. Do the quiz after each lesson before you move on: the questions are in the style of the Preliminary test.

If an explanation is not clear, ask under that lesson.
